- **Needs two:** kizufak–gitazos, kizufak–dopini, gitazos–dopini.

Either way, my last test can split the remaining group again.

I need to correct an earlier mistake. After the second test, I listed dopini–taluman as a needs-one case. Taluman was on the machine when it stayed dark, so it can't be a nexiom if the machine needs one. The correct case was **dopini–tegonol**.

Since gitazos and dupevir did not light up, 4 cases remain:
- **Needs one:** dopini–tegonol. This is the only remaining pair that includes neither gitazos, dupevir, kizufak nor taluman.
- **Needs two:** kizufak–gitazos, kizufak–dopini, gitazos–dopini.

A single test has only two outcomes, so I can't pin down one case out of 4. The best I can do is split them 2/2 and then guess between two, for a 50% chance.

- **Stays dark:** needs two with kizufak–gitazos or gitazos–dopini.

TEST: kizufak, dopini
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

After the final test, two cases fit all four results equally well:
- **Needs one, dopini–tegonol:** dopini lit up tests 1 and 4. Tegonol was never tested, and no other object was on the machine during the dark tests.
- **Needs two, kizufak–dopini:** both were present in tests 1 and 4, and never together in the dark tests.

No other case fits. In a needs-one machine, every object from the dark tests is ruled out (kizufak, taluman, gitazos, dupevir), and test 1 requires dopini. In a needs-two machine, both nexioms must be in test 4, so the pair must be kizufak–dopini.

The tests can't separate these two, so this is a 50% guess. I'm choosing the needs-two case.

ANSWER: nexioms = kizufak, dopini; needs = two
